newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futuris says has 80.2 pct of Elders.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futuris says has 80.2 pct of Elders.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Futuris Corp said on Friday that it held 80.22 percent of takeover target Elders Australia Ltd, ahead of the official close of its offer on September 16.
"It is too early for me to comment at this stage whether we will get to 100 percent or not," Futuris company secretary Lawrence Clark told Reuters.
"Certainly we have got into our target range ... we had indicated to the market previously that we hoped to get into the 75-85 percent range," he said.

Futuris and Elders originally proposed a merger, but the move was stymied by overseas investors General Oriental Investments Ltd (GOIL) and Marathon Asset Management, which hold a combined stake of around 15 percent in Elders and were critical of merging the pastoral and industrial businesses.
Asked if Futuris had any indication GOIL or Marathon would sell their stakes, Clark said: "We have no indication to that effect".

There has been market speculation that acceptances from Elders shareholders may leave fewer than the 300 shareholders each holding stakes worth A$2,000 or more required for listing under Australian Stock Exchange regulations.
Clark said currently "discounting the employee shareholders, there are slightly less than 600 left on the register."
On September 2, saying institutional shareholders had requested more time, Futuris extended its unconditional bid by another two weeks, to close on September 16.

Asked whether a decision would be made to further extend the offer, Clark said the company would review its position on Monday "after we have seen what acceptances come in and make a decision at that stage".
